title: Director of Quality Improvement Strategy
text:
**About CCNC:**

From the mountains to the coast, from large cities to small towns, Community Care of North Carolina is transforming health care. Informed by statewide data and predictive analytics, community-based care-managers work with local physicians and diverse teams of health professionals to develop whole-person plans of care that connect people to the right local resources and increase equity and access to high quality care.

**CCNC Mission Statement**

To improve the health and quality of life for all North Carolinians by building supporting better community-based healthcare delivery systems.

**Position Summary**
====================

The Director of Quality Improvement (QI) Strategy is responsible for setting the vision for the organization’s Quality Improvement strategy, in collaboration with the Population Health Division and aligned with CCNC’s mission and strategic goals. The aim of the QI strategy is to ensure the CCPN member practices deliver high - quality health care that drives successful performance of the Clinically Integrated Network (CIN).

The Director of Quality Improvement (QI) Strategy in coordination with the Clinical Performance and Practice Engagement teams, will direct, plan, implement, monitor, coordinate, and evaluate all aspects of the QI strategy and oversee daily operations to ensure that CCNC’s strategic plan is implemented. implements and informs process improvement to create standardized and streamlined processes, workflows, and education. The Director of QI Strategy provides direct supervision of the QI Specialist and the Value Based Care Program Specialist.

Responsibilities include outreach, education, training, hands-on participative leadership, and development of an increased capacity to successfully execute performance improvement across the organization. Working directly with others across the organization, The Director of Quality Improvement (QI) Strategy ensures that the elements of the QI strategy allow for coordination and collaboration of multifaceted initiatives with practices that serve our covered populations with consideration of resources, cost savings and quality. This includes providing strategic input on the development of organizational goals, to include measurement criteria and interventions for achieving the goals.

**Essential Functions**
=======================

**Operationalize QI Strategy**
------------------------------

* Direct the implementation of Quality Improvement efforts to support CCPN practices and CCNC programming in accordance with the strategic plan.
* Establish and implement the process for how PRRs utilize the QI plans to drive performance with CCPN practices.
* Facilitate the development of programs, systems, workflows, and integration efforts in alignment with CCNC and CCPN’s contractual, regulatory and quality requirements.
* Apply QI methodology, change management strategies, team facilitation, and coaching principles to achieve program effectiveness and efficiencies.
* Mentor and train on QI methodology, change management, and coaching principles (e.g. Model for Improvement, PDSA, Lean,).
* Demonstrate subject matter expertise and knowledge of payment models and their associated quality measures.
* Serve as the subject matter expert and lead for key projects and initiatives; including developing detailed work plans, assigning responsibilities, monitoring project progress and ensuring spread and sustainability.
* Assist CCPN and CCNC with future program development, creation or delegation of accountability and ownership for program roles and continuous process improvement.
* Develop annual Quality Plans with the Value Based Care Program practices in coordination with key focus areas identified by Clinical Performance.
* Represent and demonstrate our QI strategy in monthly Joint Operating Council meetings with the Value Based Care Program practices.
* Support the Practice Based Care Coordination (PBCC) program through data mining, identification of opportunities for improvement, regular practice monitoring, and ongoing training & support for the QIPS team.
* Engage and maintain collaborative relationships with the health care community, including but not limited to primary care providers, practice managers & practice team members, health departments, FQHCs and other community partners.
* Serve as Liaison on local, regional and state workgroups and collaborative efforts.
* Partner with the QI leaders for payers to establish collaborative and effective working relationships.
* Actively participate in payer meetings to represent and demonstrate our QI strategy

***Data Management, Analytics and Presentation***

* Lead QI efforts to positively impact performance and quality measures.
* Collaborate with the Clinical Performance team to use data to evaluate the effectiveness of projects across departments
* Advise leadership on project-specific data and information needs in support of staff.
* Identify areas of opportunity for CCPN practices through clinical data analysis, interpretation, & presentation.
* Lead the QI PS team to provide excellent training and support to member practices that facilitate effective use of the organization’s value-based care data platform
* In coordination with the Clinical Performance team, train on data definitions, data interpretation and data analysis
* Support all programs in achieving program goals through data analytics and quality improvement support.
* Adhere to CCNC privacy and security policies to ensure that patient and company data are properly safeguarded.

***Staff Management and Supervision***

* Provide effective leadership with respect to recruitment, selection, training, evaluation, compensation, staff development, and advocacy for the QI Strategy Team.
* Provide oversight and guidance to staff through a team approach that allows for coordinated handoffs, communication, and workflow across provider-facing staff
* Develop strategies for allocating QI resources to meet program goals and to control costs through effective use of personnel.
* Identify staff training needs and provide appropriate training opportunities.
* Complete performance evaluations.
* Utilize conflict resolution and problem-solving skills to manage issues in a timely manner.

**Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse (BSN required; MSN preferred); Social Worker (BSW required; MSW and LCSW preferred); or master's in public health or health care administration. If RN: Active, unrestricted RN license to practice in North Carolina.
* At least 5 years of Quality Improvement or relevant health care experience with responsibilities in the following areas: operational leadership, process improvement, project management, systems analysis, data analytics, and team facilitation.
* At least 3 years of supervisory or leadership experience in health care.
* NAHQ Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ)
* Lean / Six Sigma certification a plus.
* Maintain a valid NC driver’s license with current auto liability insurance.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

Excellent communication skills

* - oral, written and public speaking
* Knowledge of government, private sector and community resources
* Knowledge of and compliance with federal and state regulations applicable to the position
* Critical thinking skills, effective clinical judgment, independent decision making, and problem- solving abilities
* Skilled in establishing rapport with providers, community partners, and members
* Strong organizational and time management skills
* Demonstrated leadership skills
* Ability to work independently and function as an integral part of the team
* Expertise with Microsoft Office suite of products and comfort with database software and the internet
* Strong competence in quality improvement methodologies, principles, and recognition programs
* Ability to take “deep dives” into multiple sources of data to drive improvement
* Ability to stimulate innovative thinking & serve as a change agent
* Able to shift strategy or approach in response to the demands of a situation

**Working Conditions**

* Multiple contacts are required with providers, members, health systems and community partners to ensure effectiveness of QI and PS work; exposure to general office conditions, as well as communicable disease could occur.
* Potential for minor physical inconveniences or discomforts in the work setting, including sitting for moderate periods of time.
* Repetitive wrist motion and occasional lifting/carrying of up to 25 pounds.
* Travel required within the region and/or the state.

**Why Join Us:**
----------------

* Make a meaningful impact on youth and families across North Carolina
* Work with a supportive and collaborative care team
* Competitive Benefits Package effective first day of employment
* Opportunities for growth, training, and bonus incentives\*

**Ready to improve the health and quality of life of all North Carolinians by building and supporting better community-based health care delivery systems?**

* **Apply today and join us in delivering compassionate care that makes a difference.**
